hook: A grainy monochrome still image from an unspecified U.S. military sensor system, showing one to two small dark objects positioned above and to the right of a central crosshair reticle, submitted by the FBI to AARO as a UAP report with no accompanying mission report.
why_it_matters: This image represents one of the rare cases in the PURSUE release where imagery derived directly from a U.S. military sensor system was submitted to AARO — though it arrived pre-redacted and without a mission report, limiting investigative value. The operator's inability to positively identify the objects, combined with the absence of contextual mission data, leaves the sighting unresolved. The corrupted timestamp further degrades the evidentiary record, illustrating a recurring challenge in UAP documentation: imagery without metadata context is difficult to analyze or corroborate.

key_findings.finding: The image was altered before submission to AARO — redactions were applied to the original military imagery prior to being forwarded by the FBI, meaning the full sensor data is not available to investigators.
No mission report accompanied the image submission, leaving the operational context — including location, altitude, speed, and sensor configuration — entirely unknown.
The operator who captured the imagery was unable to positively identify the UAP, indicating the objects did not match known signatures at the time of observation.

The timestamp embedded in the image is incorrect due to the system clock not being properly set, undermining the ability to cross-reference this sighting with other data sources or correlate it with radar or other sensor tracks.

The objects appear as one to two small, dark forms just above and to the right of the reticle center in a monochrome, grainy image — consistent with a passive optical or infrared sensor output, though the sensor type is not specified.

legacy_program_connections.reasoning: The FBI explicitly submitted this image to AARO as a UAP report, making AARO the receiving and responsible investigation office for this case.
The image derives from a U.S. military sensor system with unspecified origin; historical military UAP imagery collection has ties to Wright-Patterson, though no direct connection is stated.
